A mutation that landed in a sibling would read NOT CAUGHT for the reason suites.json's header describes, so every anchor below carries enough of this function's own text to appear exactly once in the file.
the function is fifty-seven bytes of decision and this is what happens without it
the boundary is >= 1: a receiver that has merely been noticed enters phase 3
the boundary is != 0, which is how the neighbouring functions test the same field
the boundary is > 2, so the DIL and TRN2d states are the only ones that qualify
the compare is unsigned, so a negative receiver is above the boundary rather than below it
the receiver is read as a short
the V.90 arm is gated on the K56flex receiver instead
the `+ 4` is read as a sub-object, so both fields are taken four bytes low
the two pointers change places: phase 3 is entered on the K56flex block
the demodulator is entered directly, skipping the modem's own twenty-one stores
the K56flex arm goes FIRST, so it wins when both receivers are up
the second arm is not an `else`, so both can run in one call
why: K56FlexFloModem::enterPhase3FullDuplex is ONE BYTE OF CODE in the object -- a bare `ret` at 0x101d0, with no instruction touching `this` -- and is an empty body in src/pump/v90/K56FlexFloModem.cpp.  So nothing downstream of the `k56flex_receiver` test is observable to any caller: not the comparison, not the operand it reads, not the object it is handed, and not whether the arm is exclusive with the first.  This entry is the ONE representative of that whole equivalence class rather than five separate uncaught results.  WHAT IS HELD FIXED: that the callee stays empty.  The moment K56FlexFloModem gains a real enterPhase3FullDuplex, every claim in this arm becomes testable and this entry must fail.
